brief: Pitch a six-week project to let customers export their invoices to accounting software. Two accounting vendors have public APIs; one is rate limited.
strong:
# Invoice export to accounting software

## Problem

Customers retype invoices into their accounting software every month.

## Solution

A one-click export of the month's invoices to either supported vendor, using each vendor's public API.

## Rabbit holes

Vendor B limits writes to 60 per minute; a large customer's month can take over an hour, so exports run as background jobs with progress, not as a request. Tax codes differ between vendors; we map only the three codes our invoices use and fail loudly on anything else.

## No-gos

Two-way sync and historical backfill are out of scope.

## Open question

Do we need per-customer vendor credentials, or does each vendor offer an app-level grant? This decides whether week 1 includes an OAuth flow.

# Invoice export to accounting software

## Problem

Customers retype invoices into their accounting software every month.

## Solution

A one-click export of the month's invoices to either supported vendor, using each vendor's public API.

## Rabbit holes

Both vendors have well-documented, stable APIs, so integration is straightforward and will fit easily in six weeks. Vendor B's rate limit will not matter because invoices are small documents. Tax codes map cleanly between the vendors. Customers already use these vendors, so adoption is assured.

## No-gos

Two-way sync and historical backfill are out of scope.
